red_tests.failure_fingerprint: 25 failed, 1 passed against baseline source bc0530f5 (TypeError: cmd_check() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given; AttributeError: module 'jira_label_gate' has no attribute 'scope_overlap'/'scope_tokens')

correction_reason: The sequence-1 baseline froze a defective test helper. _patched() returned mock.patch.object() PATCHERS, but test_no_additional_http_calls asserted fetch.call_count on the patcher object rather than on the mock yielded by __enter__; a _patch has no call_count, so the test raised AttributeError and could never pass regardless of the implementation. This is a defect in the test harness, not in the contract under test. The correction replaces the tuple-of-patchers with a small _Patched context manager that exposes the live build_client/fetch_issue mocks, and updates all ten call sites. The assertion itself is unchanged and still pins the real requirement: exactly one HTTP call, no extra request for scope data. RED was re-proven honestly against the pristine baseline source (25 failed, 1 passed, exit 1) by temporarily restoring scripts/jira_label_gate.py from bc0530f5 rather than relying on the earlier run.
rationale: TDD baseline (sequence 2, supersedes bc0530f5) for KAN-181 scope-relevance validation of the Jira agent-label gate. The defect: cmd_check validated agent-* LABEL PRESENCE ONLY, so any labeled ticket satisfied the gate regardless of whether the commit had anything to do with the ticket. Real evidence: a commit citing KAN-181 passed against a stale KAN-133 key left in .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG, and KAN-133's scope (renewable leases, fencing tokens) was unrelated to the work (webhook dispatch). RED: 25 failed, 1 passed (exit 1) on the missing third cmd_check parameter and the absent scope_tokens/scope_overlap helpers. GREEN: 26 passed, with tests/test_jira_label_gate.py unchanged at 22 passed, confirming the exit-code contract (0 = labeled, 1 = exists but unlabeled, 2 = unverifiable) did not regress. Design: a WORD-OVERLAP heuristic, so it can only ever add a [WARN] line naming BOTH the ticket summary and the commit subject; it never changes a return value, because a heuristic false positive must not block legitimate work. Ticket keys and agent-* roster labels are stripped before tokenizing so a ticket cannot 'match' a commit merely by repeating the same key or lane. The summary field is already present in the existing fetch_issue response (fields=labels,summary,status), so no additional HTTP request was introduced; test_no_additional_http_calls pins fetch_issue.call_count == 1. Missing or boilerplate-only input returns None, which callers treat as silence rather than mismatch. All warning output is ASCII-folded and clipped per the scripts/AGENTS.md rule.
